headline: Executive order moves federal agencies toward buying common goods and services through one central agency to cut costs.
what_it_does: This order directs federal agencies to combine, or consolidate, how they buy common goods and services. The official title says the goal is to reduce waste and save taxpayer money. Based on the title, purchasing that is now spread across many agencies would be handled in a more centralized way. The likely central buyer is the General Services Administration (GSA), but no summary was provided to confirm the details.

who_it_affects.how: Agencies may lose some control over buying common items and services and may need to go through a central buyer instead.
Their jobs and work processes may change as buying is combined across agencies.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that sell to the federal government
who_it_affects.how: Contractors may need to work through a more centralized buying system rather than with individual agencies.
The order states its aim is to lower government spending by reducing duplicate purchasing.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed March 20, 2025; executive orders generally take effect when signed, though specific steps may have later deadlines.
